chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from Sandal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One who recites Surah al-Dhariyat during his day or his night, Allah will improve his livelihood, grant him abundant sustenance, and illuminate his grave with a lamp that shines until the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for reciting Surah al-Dhariyat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith links the recitation of Surah al-Dhariyat to both worldly provision (*rizq wasi'*) and otherworldly illumination (*nur fi al-qabr*). It reflects the Shia tradition of viewing Quranic recitation as a means to rectify one's livelihood and prepare the soul for the Barzakh, emphasizing the transformative power of the Surah's themes of divine power and resurrection.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from Sandal from Dawud b. Farqad from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

One who keeps reciting Surah Zariyat in the day or night, Allah would improve the means of his livelihood and grant him much livelihood and also light up his grave with such a lamp that would keep burning and giving out light upto the Day of Judgment.
